      "observed": "D30 pin 4 (A2, anode of the second LED channel) is on ESTOP_OUT. R60 (130R) runs from D30 pin 2 (K2) to ESTOP_OUT. Channel 2 therefore forms a closed loop ESTOP_OUT -> LED -> R60 -> ESTOP_OUT with no supply or ground reference, so the channel can never light. Channel 1 is wired correctly: A1 (pin 3) is on LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV and K1 goes through R59 to GND.",
      "expected": "Channel 2 should mirror channel 1: its anode should sit on the 3.3 V LED supply net LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, with its cathode resistor R60 driving the status signal ESTOP_OUT. As wired, the anode and the resistor end share a net and the LED is dead.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"A1\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"K2\") (pintype \"input\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The second status LED of the e-stop indicator (D30 channel 2) never lights. Operators lose a visual e-stop/ESTOP_OUT indication, though the e-stop function on ESTOP_OUT itself is unaffected.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["U31"],
      "pins": ["U31.2", "U31.3"],
      "nets": ["GND"],
      "observed": "LSM6DS3 auxiliary I2C pins SDX (pin 2) and SCX (pin 3) are tied to the GND net rather than being left open or pulled to VDDIO.",
      "expected": "The auxiliary master-interface pins of the LSM6DS3 should be left unconnected (or pulled up), not hard-tied to ground, unless the reference design says otherwise.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U31\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"SDX\") (pintype \"bidirectional\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U31\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"SCX\") (pintype \"input\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "Possibly harmless if the part's aux interface is unused, but it can disturb the IMU's auxiliary bus and is not normal practice.",
      "confidence": 0.2
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely anomaly is the second e-stop status LED channel (D30): its anode A2 sits on ESTOP_OUT together with its series resistor R60, forming a self-loop that can never light, while channel 1 is wired correctly to the 3.3 V LED supply. The remaining passives, supply rails and interfaces checked against the netlist and SPICE deck are consistent."
}

anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2, anode of the second LED channel) is on ESTOP_OUT. R60 (130R) runs from D30 pin 2 (K2) to ESTOP_OUT. Channel 2 therefore forms a closed loop ESTOP_OUT -> LED -> R60 -> ESTOP_OUT with no supply or ground reference, so the channel can never light. Channel 1 is wired correctly: A1 (pin 3) is on LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV and K1 goes through R59 to GND.
anomalies.expected: Channel 2 should mirror channel 1: its anode should sit on the 3.3 V LED supply net LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, with its cathode resistor R60 driving the status signal ESTOP_OUT. As wired, the anode and the resistor end share a net and the LED is dead.
anomalies.impact: The second status LED of the e-stop indicator (D30 channel 2) never lights. Operators lose a visual e-stop/ESTOP_OUT indication, though the e-stop function on ESTOP_OUT itself is unaffected.

anomalies.observed: LSM6DS3 auxiliary I2C pins SDX (pin 2) and SCX (pin 3) are tied to the GND net rather than being left open or pulled to VDDIO.
anomalies.expected: The auxiliary master-interface pins of the LSM6DS3 should be left unconnected (or pulled up), not hard-tied to ground, unless the reference design says otherwise.
anomalies.impact: Possibly harmless if the part's aux interface is unused, but it can disturb the IMU's auxiliary bus and is not normal practice.
